pluss::series::print¶

Back to Series Factory API Reference

Signature¶

pluss::series::print(const Series& s) -> std::string

pluss::series::print(const Series& s,
                     const PrintOptions& opt) -> std::string

pluss::series::print(std::ostream& os,
                     const Series& s,
                     const PrintOptions& opt = {}) -> std::ostream&

What It Does¶

pluss::series::print(...) renders a Series in the readable aligned layout used throughout these handwritten docs.

This page lives in the factory reference because print(...) is a free function on the public pluss::series::* surface, not a Series method.

Use it when you want one of two things:

  • a printable std::string

  • direct output to a stream such as std::cout

It never mutates the Series. It is a presentation tool.

The distinction matters:

  • pluss::series::print(series) returns a string

  • pluss::series::print(std::cout, series) writes immediately to the stream

So if you call pluss::series::print(series) and do nothing with the returned string, nothing is printed yet.

Overload Map¶

print(s)

Returns the default formatted rendering as a std::string.

print(s, opt)

Returns a std::string using the caller’s formatting policy.

print(os, s, opt)

Writes directly to a stream and returns that stream so the call chains naturally with << "\n".

Parameters¶

os (std::ostream&)

The destination stream for the stream-writing overload.

Use this form when printing is the final side effect rather than an intermediate string.

s (const Series&)

The Series to render.

The function reads the current shape, dtype, platform, and values without changing them.

opt (const PrintOptions&)

Formatting policy.

The option surface is wide, but the usage model is easier if you group the toggles:

  • metadata toggles control whether shape, dtype, platform, strides, and other header details are shown

  • content toggles decide whether you see header only, values only, or both

  • numeric toggles control general/fixed/scientific rendering, precision, and trimming

  • boolean toggles choose between true/false and 1/0

  • pretty-layout toggles control alignment, bracket style, slice labels, summarization, and line wrapping

That means PrintOptions changes how the data is shown, not what the data is.

Returns¶

std::string For the string-returning overloads.

std::ostream& For the stream-writing overload.

Examples¶

Example 1. The simplest overload returns a formatted string.

auto printable = pluss::make_series({
    {1.25, 2.5, 3.75},
    {4.0, 5.5, 6.25},
});

auto rendered = pluss::series::print(printable);
std::cout << rendered;

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 1.2500 2.5000 3.7500 ⎤
⎣ 4.0000 5.5000 6.2500 ⎦

Example 2. The stream overload writes directly to std::cout.

pluss::series::print(std::cout, printable);

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 1.2500 2.5000 3.7500 ⎤
⎣ 4.0000 5.5000 6.2500 ⎦

Example 3. std::cout << series is also valid, because Series has stream support too.

std::cout << printable;

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡ 1.2500 2.5000 3.7500 ⎤
⎣ 4.0000 5.5000 6.2500 ⎦

Example 4. You can hide the metadata block and keep the data rendering.

pluss::PrintOptions opt;
opt.metadata_mode = pluss::codem::PrintMetadataMode::None;

auto rendered = pluss::series::print(printable, opt);
std::cout << rendered;

Output¶

data=
⎡ 1.2500 2.5000 3.7500 ⎤
⎣ 4.0000 5.5000 6.2500 ⎦

Example 5. Boolean output can be rendered in compact 1/0 form.

pluss::PrintOptions opt;
opt.bool_style = pluss::codem::PrintBoolStyle::OneZero;

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({true, false, true, true}, pluss::ScalarType::Bool),
    opt);

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 0, 1, 1]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • print(...) is for human-readable display, not stable machine interchange.

  • Hiding metadata changes presentation only. It does not turn the output into a raw numeric dump.

  • print(series) does not print by itself. It returns a string that you still need to store, stream, or otherwise use.

  • std::cout << series also works, but pluss::series::print(...) is the explicit public print facility when you want to control formatting.

Summary¶

Use pluss::series::print(...) when you want the public rendering surface for Series.

  • choose print(s) when you need a string

  • choose print(os, s, ...) for direct stream output

  • std::cout << series is the shorthand stream route when you do not need custom print options

  • use PrintOptions to tune presentation without changing the data

See Also¶

  • pluss::series::make: construct a Series to print.

  • pluss::series::select: build a new Series by conditional branch selection before printing it.
